name: Centenary Partners Fund

funder.name: Norfolk Wildlife Trust (funded by nine business Centenary Partners)

summary: Small-grant fund for Norfolk community and conservation groups, CICs and small charities to create, maintain or protect spaces for nature, including tools, equipment and restoration projects.
reporting: A short end-of-project report, usually due within 1 to 2 months of completion, covering how the money was spent, how many people benefited and the outcomes achieved.

eligibility.rule: Activities and projects are primarily within Norfolk
Annual turnover or funding does not exceed £100,000
Supports Norfolk Wildlife Trust's charitable objectives
Maintains a valid governing document throughout the grant
Operates a dedicated bank account with two independent signatories
Has safeguarding policies and checks when activities involve vulnerable people

effort.quote: Our Centenary Partners Fund opens for applications on Monday 2 November 2026, and the closing deadline is Friday 22 January 2027.

eligibility.quote: Are carrying out activities and projects primarily within Norfolk.
Have a turnover or funding that does not exceed £100,000 per annum.
Support the charitable objectives of Norfolk Wildlife Trust.
Your group must maintain a valid governing document (such as a constitution, set of rules, or articles of association) throughout the life of the grant.
You must operate a dedicated organisational bank account requiring at least two independent (unrelated) signatories for withdrawals or online transactions.
If your activities involve children, young people, or vulnerable adults, you must have a suitable safeguarding policy and proper checks (e.g. DBS checks) in place.

after_award.quote: You must complete and return a short end of project/monitoring report by the deadline specified in our offer letter (typically within 1 to 2 months of project completion).
